exposure: maternal obesity (BMI >= 30 kg/m2), categorized into Group A (BMI 30-34.9 kg/m2) and Group B (BMI >= 35 kg/m2)
cohort: The study included 178 pregnant women with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher, recruited from the Hayatabad Medical Complex.
finding: Higher degrees of maternal obesity (BMI >= 35 kg/m2) are significantly associated with increased rates of maternal complications (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, cesarean section, wound infection) and neonatal complications (macrosomia, low Apgar scores, NICU admissions) compared to lower degrees of obesity (BMI 30-34.9 kg/m2).
mod_finding: Higher degrees of maternal obesity (BMI >= 35 kg/m2) were significantly associated with a higher rate of cesarean delivery (62.2%) compared to lower degrees of obesity (40.6%).
